title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: The briefing correctly distinguishes the planned labelled-upload capability from today's documented encrypted-file restriction. Its roadmap facts, billing rates and existing controls are supported; two control paths stop early on the correct configuration page and should be extended.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans support for uploading Purview sensitivity-labelled files to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the Microsoft 365 channel.
claims.quote: Unblock users from upload files with Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MPIP) sensitivity labels to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the M365 channel.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet have a page documenting the planned labelled-upload feature's behaviour.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The existing file-input documentation says encrypted files, including label-encrypted and password-protected files, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: For an encrypted or password-protected Office upload, the agent can tell the user it cannot read the file.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted uploads instead return a generic error.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input page describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The file-input page directs readers to Microsoft Copilot Chat as an experience supporting sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: or use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: Connecting the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels makes an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: After you publish your agent at least once, you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing: third paragraph; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented that the related Purview encryption model applies to the planned agent uploads.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio uploaded files sensitivity label EXTRACT downstream connector DLP enforcement switch permissions. Read ai-copilot-studio, ai-m365-copilot-considerations and image-input-analysis: encryption support is SharePoint-only; no planned upload enforcement model is described.

claims.claim: For documented label-encrypted content, AI apps require both EXTRACT and VIEW to return data.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio page documents encryption support only with sensitivity labels and only for SharePoint knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting page gives the conflicting statement that the agent cannot extract or ground on encrypted file content.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file. This limitation includes sensitivity labels that apply encryption, Double Key Encryption (DKE), and password-protected files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: For Copilot generally, EXTRACT determines whether encrypted content can be displayed as text.
claims.quote: It's this usage right that determines whether Copilot or agents can display text to the user from encrypted content.

claims.claim: Full control (OWNER) includes EXTRACT.
claims.quote: Because the Full control (OWNER) usage right includes all the usage rights, EXTRACT is automatically included with Full control.

claims.claim: User-defined label encryption ordinarily prevents Copilot and agents from accessing unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: A default label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents is an exception, provided the user has EXTRACT.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.claim: Directly referencing a document by typing '/' is the other documented exception, also requiring EXTRACT.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Credits measure agent effort retrieving information, responding to prompts and using actions.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.claim: The base feature rate for a generative answer is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.claim: The premium text and generative AI tools reasoning-model meter is 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 billed tokens.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are calculated from the exact number of billed tokens, at 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 tokens.

claims.claim: For reasoning models, the premium token meter is additional to the operation's feature rate.
claims.quote: Total cost = feature rate for the operation + text and generative AI tools (premium) for the reasoning model's token usage.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for Microsoft 365 Copilot users when the agent uses their authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.claim: The premium reasoning meter has the documented inclusion for authenticated, Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed employee-facing agent usage.
claims.quote: | - Text and generative AI tools (premium)^5^ | 10 Copilot Credits per 1,000 tokens | No charge |

claims.claim: Makers configure existing uploads per agent at Settings > Generative AI > File processing capabilities > File uploads.
claims.quote: Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI. ... Navigate to the File processing capabilities section. ... Turn on File uploads.

claims.claim: The printed Purview DLP path reaches the Copilot location on the policy wizard's Locations page.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels'. The existing path reaches the correct location but stops before selecting the label condition documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule calls create a Copilot policy and a label-based rule blocking content processing.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences") ... New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The rule's label condition is Content contains > Sensitivity labels, with location and advanced-rule variables defined as in the reference example.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: The printed sensitivity-label editing path reaches the Access control page for label encryption.
claims.quote: make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected for the label's scope ... on the Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected page ... select Control access. ... On the Access control page
claims.fix: Extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now'. Keep the EXTRACT note. The entry route and scope step are supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels; the additional options are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/encryption-sensitivity-labels.

claims.claim: On Access control, Configure access control settings followed by Assign permissions now enables administrator-defined encryption permissions.
claims.quote: When you select Configure access control settings on the Access control page to create or edit a sensitivity label, choose ... Assign permissions now, so that you can determine exactly which users get which permissions

claims.claim: The Purview UI displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: Set-Label with Identity, EncryptionEnabled $true, EncryptionProtectionType Template and EncryptionRightsDefinitions sets template-based label encryption rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have ... This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.claim: The Purview portal route to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive is Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now:

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables sensitivity-label support for SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

claims.claim: The portal route for enabling SharePoint and OneDrive label support requires a global administrator.
claims.quote: This option is the easiest way to enable sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive. You must sign in as a global administrator for your tenant.

claims.claim: Multi-Geo tenants must use PowerShell to enable label support in all their geo-locations.
claims.quote: If you have Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo, you must use PowerShell to enable these capabilities for all your geo-locations.
